source_facts: Verdant Patch 1.7 is a synthetic greenhouse observation tool; these facts are authoritative. This tutorial is a supervised training exercise for research assistants, not a live irrigation procedure. The training station is bench-4. Before starting capture, the assistant must have an active trainee session and the probe must have completed a dry calibration during the current session. An instructor supplies the session through the station login screen. A previous session's calibration is insufficient. Set the probe in its empty cradle and run `vpatch calibrate --station bench-4 --dry`; successful completion displays `calibrated`. A failed calibration blocks capture and is referred to the instructor. The capture command is `vpatch capture --station bench-4 --tray basil-demo --samples 6`. The sample count is the number of readings per pot, not the number of pots. There are three labeled pots in basil-demo, so the exercise produces eighteen readings. The probe remains in place until capture finishes. Capture creates a local survey but does not publish it. In the fixed training example the resulting survey identifier is sv-demo-41; a real exercise must use its returned identifier in subsequent commands. A reading is one probe measurement. A survey is the collection of readings from one capture. Inspect the captured survey with `vpatch inspect --survey sv-demo-41`. Its `spread` field is the difference between the highest and lowest readings for one pot, expressed in percentage points. A pot passes when spread is at most 4 percentage points. The example readings 31, 33, 32, 34, 32, 31 yield spread 3 and pass. A failed pot requires an instructor's decision before any repeat capture; trainees do not discard it and retry independently. Export the inspected survey using `vpatch export --survey sv-demo-41 --format csv`; this writes a local CSV containing readings and pot labels. Export is not a publication operation. Record the returned survey identifier in the lab notebook so the notebook can be connected to the CSV. This tool does not control irrigation. The page must preserve useful links to `lab-session.md` for station login, `probe-care.md` for handling the probe, and `survey-columns.md` for CSV field definitions. These are supplemental links: the facts necessary to complete this exercise are supplied here. Presentation may change within this tutorial, but the exercise must not expand to production greenhouse work.

# Verdant Patch: your first bench survey

This supervised exercise gives greenhouse research assistants a small dataset they can inspect and discuss with an instructor. Use the labeled basil-demo tray at bench-4 throughout the exercise. The CSV and your notebook entry will describe the same survey, making it possible to revisit a particular pot without guessing which capture produced the observations.

## Take the readings

Run `vpatch capture --station bench-4 --tray basil-demo --samples 6`. Keep the probe in place until capture finishes. In this training example, the returned identifier is `sv-demo-41`. Your own exercise may return a different identifier; carry that value into the later commands rather than copying the example identifier automatically.

The tray has three labeled pots. The six samples produce eighteen readings across the tray. Keep the labels attached to their pots so the exported data remains useful during the discussion. Handling guidance is available in [Probe care](probe-care.md).

## Finish with a file

After inspecting the survey, run `vpatch export --survey sv-demo-41 --format csv`. This writes a local CSV containing the readings and pot labels. Record the returned survey identifier in your lab notebook. The identifier connects your written observations to the file when the instructor looks at the exercise later.

## A bench example

For one pot, consider the six readings 31, 33, 32, 34, 32, and 31. The resulting spread is 3, and this pot passes. A trainee can keep this example beside the inspection output when comparing the measurements from the demonstration tray. The numbers are an illustration, not values that every basil pot is expected to produce.

## Session materials

Before starting capture, sign in with an active trainee session. The instructor supplies that session through the station login screen; [Lab session](lab-session.md) describes the screen used at the bench. A dry calibration must have completed successfully during this same session. Calibration from a previous session does not satisfy the exercise prerequisite.

Set the probe in its empty cradle and run `vpatch calibrate --station bench-4 --dry`. Success displays `calibrated`. If calibration fails, do not start capture; ask the instructor to resolve the failure.

## What the collection represents

A reading is one measurement from the probe. A survey is the collection of readings from one capture. The `--samples` value counts readings per pot, not pots in the tray. Capture creates the survey locally and does not publish it.

## Inspect the result

Run `vpatch inspect --survey sv-demo-41` with your returned survey identifier. A pot passes when its spread is at most 4 percentage points. If a pot fails, get the instructor's decision before making another capture. Do not discard the result and repeat the exercise independently to obtain a passing set.

The CSV field descriptions are in [Survey columns](survey-columns.md). Exporting the CSV is also local; it does not publish the survey.

## Measurement vocabulary

The inspection field `spread` is the difference between a pot's highest and lowest readings, expressed in percentage points. It describes variation within that pot's sample set rather than the number of pots in the survey. Verdant Patch observes the tray and does not control irrigation. This page covers the training bench only.
